name: De Vinne 12pt 1897
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office; 1897 stock mark Keystone–10
description: Twelve-point De Vinne with flared serifs, a sweeping Q tail, double-storey a and g, and observed mixed-height figures. Nine named alternates retain source variations.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures, with period, comma, right single quotation mark and the double-bar historical hyphen encoded as hyphen-minus. Space has a modern layout advance. Nine observed alternatives are unencoded glyphs available through stylistic sets; no unsupported character is inferred. Nine whole observed diagonal fractions, cent and percent are also encoded. Fraction row-center placement is a modern layout convention, independent of historical baseline evidence.
observed: The 1897 specimen supplies both complete twelve-point alphabets. Matching census and job-room impressions supply clearer letters, all ten figures and punctuation. The census M and seven differently shaped or positioned figures are retained as named alternatives. The census ten-figure row is the default set; its unequal positions are preserved. Matching ATF assortments supply whole 12-point diagonal fractions and symbols; exact selected pages, crops, thresholds and scale measurements are retained. A broad, flatter S appears beside a narrow S in the BYU twelve-point poster and repeats in the Handy specimen. The complete BYU broad impression is retained as an unencoded alternate.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform source-page scaling, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. No cross-size substitution or independent width stretching. Fraction row-center placement at 350 is a modern layout choice; no historical text baseline is established by the charts. No fraction parts are assembled or redrawn.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann
revival.notes: All visible forms are observed. Uniform source-page scales and measured rigid row rotations preserve optical proportions. Nine named alternatives use ss01/ss02/ss03/ss04; ss04 selects the broad S. Both distant numeral blocks have independently measured baselines. The document specimen is comparison-only. See source/METHOD.md for reproduction and feature use. The whole fraction companions retain their full physical source dimensions and deliberate slash interruptions. Existing outlines, spacing and named alternatives are preserved.
